quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. They tell you traffic rules. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: To help drivers merge from an entrance ramp into your lane, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Merge into the next lane, if possible.
Not worry about it, since they are the ones trying to merge.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into the next lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Give them space to safely merge by moving to a different lane if you can.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
Travel at a faster speed than usual to get to your destination more quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Decrease your following distance so you can be as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Always be flexible about your lane position, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies in poor conditions.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should not:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid sudden moves.
Use both brakes.
Brake quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake quickly.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently. Do not brake quickly.

questions.question: If you are transporting a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean as you lean.
Hold onto the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean as you lean.
questions.explanation: A passenger should lean with you during turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control. They should hold onto passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: To be effective, a face shield should not:

options.text: Be free of scratches.
Allow clear views to both sides.
Be airtight.
Fasten securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be airtight.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, protect against impact, allow clear side views, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. An airtight shield causes fogging and makes it hard to see.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.
Use your high beam light, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to avoid collisions. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Use your high beam, except when following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: A windshield:

options.text: Is a good substitute for a face shield.
Does not completely protect your eyes from the wind.
Is required on all motorcycles.
Should be used on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not completely protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield does not provide enough protection for your eyes. Use goggles or a face shield instead. Most windshields will not keep wind out of your eyes.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your eyes focused on the front of the motorcycle.
Look ahead to where you want to go through the turn.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Speed up before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead to where you want to go through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: For normal braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Alternate between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking alcohol, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for your friend.
Keep your friend busy with other activities.
Stop your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Let your friend ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let your friend ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: You can prevent someone from riding while impaired by arranging another way for them to get home, involving them in other activities to slow their drinking, keeping them from leaving before they are sober, and getting help from other friends.

questions.question: What is a benefit of a shatter-resistant face shield?

options.text: It protects a rider's face during a crash.
It only protects riders from dirt.
It does not protect as well as goggles.
It should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects a rider's face during a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield also shields you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until the motorcycle stops.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of proper riding clothing?

options.text: It protects a rider in a crash.
It makes a rider look cool.
Style is more important than protection.
It should be loose and baggy.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects a rider in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothing protects you in a crash. It should be made of sturdy, bright, and reflective materials. Clothes should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough to allow free movement.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Is braking in a turn easier or harder than braking on a straight road?

options.text: It is easier than braking on a straight road.
It is harder than braking on a straight road.
It is safe to use only the front brake.
It is safe to use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes in a turn, but you must know the correct technique and be very careful.

questions.question: Which action should you NOT do to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Use your high beam headlight when possible.
Keep a greater distance from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, use your high beam headlight when not near other vehicles, and keep more distance from other vehicles. Watch vehicles ahead because their headlights help light the road and their taillights show bumps.

questions.question: The body eliminates one drink per hour. If someone had eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks
Four drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: To find how much alcohol remains, subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. In this case, about four drinks would remain.

questions.question: Which option offers the best protection?

options.text: Sunglasses
Windshield
Goggles
Face shield

questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding next to another rider?

options.text: Allows you to maximize the surface of the road.
It limits your escape routes.
Allows you to communicate with one another.
Makes it easier for other motorists to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to another motorcyclist. This reduces the escape options for both riders if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you assume?

options.text: Motorcycles are as easy to see as other vehicles.
Other drivers cannot see you.
You do not need to make sure other drivers see you.
You should ride aggressively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles, making them hard to see. Ride defensively and assume others do not see you.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, how should they do it?

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a pyramid formation.
One at a time.
In a splintered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The next rider should wait until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before passing.
